transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-01-28
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Samir Patel (Argosy VP Eng), Dana Li (Argosy SRE), Maya Roberts (Product), Oliver Grant (CTO), Zoe Kim (SecOps)

Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): Quick follow-up after last week's incident where Argosy saw elevated latency and token failures on the hosted Redwood endpoints. Focused on RCA, what was patched, and validation plan.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time, appreciate it. we'll keep this tight  agenda is quick RCA review, what we patched, and next steps. Samir you okay to kick off with how things looked from Argosy side?
[00:18] Samir (Argosy VP Eng): Yeah thanks, Jordan. So last Tuesday about 09:20 PST we started seeing 95th+ tail latency spike and some downstream request errors. It correlated with a traffic spike from our batch job, umm  we hadn't expected that pattern. A bunch of requests hit the hosted endpoint, latency climbed to 3\u20134s on average and some timeouts.
[00:36] Dana (SRE): There were a number of 5xxs too. We traced to increased KV cache evictions on your side? we saw huge eviction rate and then a cascade of cold cache misses, which blew up CPU on model servers.
[00:52] Priya (Redwood SE): Right  our telemetry showed a rapid increase in KV cache churn and simultaneous autoscaler scale down events on a subset of the pool. The combination caused a bunch of in-flight requests to hit colder model variants and higher-latency kernels. We also found a routing config that routed to a lower-capacity variant under certain cost-tier fallback rules  that routing rule should not have matched for Argosy's account.
[01:15] Zoe (SecOps): Quick Q  was there any data exposure? logs or payloads persisted?
[01:22] Priya (Redwood SE): Good question. We checked storage and logs: user payloads were not logged beyond ephemeral traces. No S3 artifacts or audit anomalies. The main issue was performance and error rates, not data leakage.
[01:35] Oliver (CTO): So the root cause is twofold  cache eviction under load and an incorrect routing predicate?
[01:41] Priya (Redwood SE): That's a neat summary, yes. The eviction was due to a default KV cache size that we tuned down on the shared pool months ago to reduce memory pressure. Under your sudden access pattern the eviction rate skyrocketed. Simultaneously, the routing policy we deploy for cross-account cost fallbacks had an edge-case match when certain tags were missing from requests  your traffic matched that edge case and got routed to a cheaper variant.
[02:05] Samir (Argosy VP Eng): Oof. Ok. How did you mitigate? we saw you pushed something Sunday?
[02:12] Jordan (Redwood AE): Right  quick recap of mitigation: Priya's team temporarily increased KV cache max entries for Argosy's pool, disabled the fallback rule for your account, and adjusted the autoscaler threshold to avoid aggressive scale-down during short-lived spikes. We also rolled a small patch to add eviction logging so we can trace it earlier.
[02:35] Priya (Redwood SE): We also added a short-term circuit that pins to the warm variant if eviction rate > X for > 30s  it's a bandaid but prevents the cold-miss cascade.
[02:48] Dana (SRE): I saw the pin; it dropped the error rate quickly. Latency improved within 12 minutes of the patch.
[02:55] Maya (Product): Appreciate that. From product side we need an assurance this won't recur during predictable traffic bursts (billing run, sync jobs).
[03:04] Priya (Redwood SE): Totally. Longer-term fixes we're planning: increase KV cache footprint for dedicated pools, improve routing predicate validation so tags are required, and add more conservative autoscaler cooldowns for variability-prone accounts.
[03:20] Jordan (Redwood AE): And to be clear, for Argosy we proposed a config that includes a higher KV cache cap, a permanent exclusion from the cost-fallback routing, and a more conservative scale-down policy. We'll share the config diff.
[03:33] Samir (Argosy): Sounds fine. One concern  cost. If we increase cache sizes and disable cost fallbacks, that ups the bill. We need visibility on the cost delta.
[03:41] Jordan (Redwood AE): Understood  we'll include a cost projection with the config diff; also we'll apply credits for the incident window and discuss a commitment level if you prefer a Dedicated pool.
[03:52] Oliver (CTO): Can you outline what monitoring and alerting changes you will make so our SREs are alerted earlier? We want precise SLO-oriented alerts, not generic noise.
[04:02] Priya (Redwood SE): We'll add eviction-rate alerts (per-account), KV miss ratio, and a routing-rule mismatch alert. We'll tune thresholds to your traffic profile. We'll also hook into your PagerDuty escalation if you want.
[04:17] Zoe (SecOps): And for change control  how do we prevent a config rollback from reintroducing the fallback?
[04:22] Priya (Redwood SE): We're going to add an account-level policy flag that prevents the fallback rule from being applied unless explicitly enabled. That flag is in the access control layer and requires infra-owner approval to change.
[04:32] Dana (SRE): Nice. On logs, Jordan, you mentioned trimmed debug logs  could you share those and the exact window for our team to compare with our traces?
[04:40] Jordan (Redwood AE): Yes, we'll send the trimmed logs (no PII) and a timeline slide. Expect that by end of day Thursday.
[04:47] Samir (Argosy): Good. What's the validation plan? How do we run the load testing without impacting prod?
[04:53] Priya (Redwood SE): Plan: stage cluster with production equivalent model variants and config, run a 2-hour load test that mirrors the batch job traffic in a ramp pattern. We'll coordinate throttles and abort conditions. If that passes, we'll schedule a safe window to apply config to production.
[05:08] Maya (Product): About SLA  we want to reopen the SLA conversation, incident credits were helpful but given risk profile we may want a dedicated capacity offer.
[05:16] Jordan (Redwood AE): Happy to discuss Dedicated pricing and commit tiers. We'll include a side-by-side of predicted unit cost after the config changes vs Dedicated baseline.
[05:25] Priya (Redwood SE): One more technical note: we also found a minor bug in the autoscaler cooldown logic that could trigger scale-down sooner than intended when metrics were sparse for short intervals. We patched it in canary and will roll to the pool after testing.
[05:40] Dana (SRE): Are you going to backfill metrics for the 24h around the incident? That would help reconstruct what happened.
[05:46] Priya (Redwood SE): Yes, we extracted 48 hours of metrics so you can align. We'll attach CPU, KV evictions, miss ratio, and routing decisions.
[05:52] Samir (Argosy): Okay, let's talk timeline: when do you want us to sign off on the staging test and the config push?
[05:57] Jordan (Redwood AE): Ideally we run staging test 2025-02-04, then production push 2025-02-06 pending results. But we can be flexible.
[06:05] Oliver (CTO): Works for me. Dana will coordinate on exact test parameters.
[06:09] Dana (SRE): Yep.
[06:11] Lena (CSM): I'll get a calendar invite for the 02/04 test and attach the runbook and incident timeline.
[06:18] Samir (Argosy): Thanks. A couple quick asks: 1) please make the routing predicate docs shareable to our infra team, 2) can we get an exec-level one-pager for our CTO about risk/mitigation?
[06:27] Jordan (Redwood AE): Yes to both  routing docs and an exec summary, we'll send.
[06:32] Zoe (SecOps): And for compliance  any change to logging or audit trails we should be aware of? You said no PII was in logs, but will the new eviction logging include any user identifiers?
[06:42] Priya (Redwood SE): Eviction logging will include request IDs and anonymized account IDs only, no user payloads. We'll show the schema before enabling.
[06:50] Maya (Product): On preventing recurrence, do you have a formal postmortem writeup? It would be helpful for our internal review to have the timeline + root cause + fix list.
[06:59] Jordan (Redwood AE): We're drafting a postmortem doc and will share a redacted copy by Friday 2025-01-31.
[07:06] Samir (Argosy): Sweet. Anything else from Redwood?
[07:09] Priya (Redwood SE): Just that we'll send the config diff and cos t projection. Apologies again for the disruption  we'll make sure this is much safer.
[07:18] Jordan (Redwood AE): From our side we'll also include a proposal for Dedicated commit if you want to evaluate.
[07:24] Oliver (CTO): Okay thanks. We'll review docs and the staging plan and come back with any questions.
[07:30] Lena (CSM): Quick recap of action items and owners: Priya increase KV cache on staging; Dana share traces; Jordan send slides and credits; Lena schedule follow-up. We'll capture these in the ticket.
[07:45] Samir (Argosy): Thanks everyone. Appreciate the fast response.
[07:49] Jordan (Redwood AE): Thank you all. We'll follow up in writing.
[07:55] Meeting end.
